correctness.rationale: Integration of the Thomas–Fermi parabola yields the stated \(F_a\). The established expansion ODE implies \(\lambda(t)\sim\sqrt2\omega t\), and the core and shell fractions are each \(O(t^{-1})\) while their product is positive and integrable on \((t_c,\infty)\). Renewal expectations give \(K(r)=r\int_0^\infty A(t)B(t)\,dt+o(r)>0\) as \(r\downarrow0\), since both separate means are \(O(r\log(1/r))\). At shell entry, the exact quadratic onset is \(B(t)=3\lambda'(t_c)^2(t-t_c)^2/(2c^2)+O((t-t_c)^3)\). One-sided Laplace analysis yields \(\mathbb E_r B\sim 3\lambda'(t_c)^2e^{-rt_c}/(c^2r^2)\), \(\mathbb E_r(AB)/\mathbb E_r B\to A(t_c)\), and \(\mathbb E_r A\to A(0)>A(t_c)\), hence the negative sharp covariance asymptotic. The mean functions are continuous in the reset rate and therefore at least one crossing exists. Independent finite quadratures and 269 numerical assertions support but do not establish the universal proof.

value.rationale: The two macroscopic disjoint counting windows form a natural spatial diagnostic distinguishing core depletion from newly arrived shell mass. The sign switch is a qualitative departure from uniform intuitive attraction under shared resetting, and occurs in every geometry with \(0<u<1<c<v\). The exact weak-rate integral and strong-rate onset constant predict the observable crossover scales; the strong-rate leading coefficient is independent of the far shell boundary. This goes beyond correctness or a minor coefficient, while not pretending to solve the full finite-particle quantum problem.
